title: Houses 4/9: Placidus, Koch, Gauquelin-36 (P/K/G) — Newton iteration
description:
### Summary
Add the iterative semi-arc systems: Placidus (default, P), Koch (K), and Gauquelin 36-sectors (G). Placidus and Gauquelin share an identical Newton-iteration skeleton (extract a shared helper). All three fall back to Porphyry inside the polar circle. G produces 36 cusps (`cusps[1..=36]`), the only system that does.

### Files
- `src/houses.rs` — replace the stub arms for Placidus (the `_` default arm → Placidus), Koch, Gauquelin in `calc_h`; add `fn placidus_newton_cusp(rectasc: f64, fh_init: f64, divisor: f64, sine, cose, tane, tanfi, geolat) -> NewtonOutcome` shared by P and G (ref §5 default + G). Define an enum/result capturing {converged cusp + converged `f` (for the AscDash speed), or DegenerateAxis (cusp=rectasc, speed=armc_speed), or NonConverged (→ Porphyry)}.
- `tests/c-gen/gen_houses.c` — add `"iterative"` and `"gauquelin36"` keys.
- `tests/golden-data/houses.json` — regenerate.
- `tests/golden/houses.rs` — add `iterative` and `gauquelin36` tests.

### Implementation steps
Read `docs/c-ref-houses.md` §5 "K", "G", "Default — Placidus", and §4.2(a), §12.7 (convergence uses `diff_degrees`, not raw subtraction).
1. **Shared Newton helper** `placidus_newton_cusp` — ref §5 "Default — Placidus" per-cusp loop AND §5 "G" loop (they are the same skeleton; Gauquelin's divisor is `9/ih2`, Placidus's is fixed `3` or `1.5`). Steps: seed `tant` from `tand(asind(sine*sind(asc1(rectasc, fh_init,...))))`; if `|tant|<VERY_SMALL` → DegenerateAxis (cusp=rectasc, speed=ARMCS). Else compute `f=atand(sind(asind(tanfi*tant)/divisor)/tant)`, `cusp=asc1(rectasc,f,...)`, then loop `i=1..=NITER_MAX`: recompute `tant` from the current cusp, recompute `f`, recompute cusp; converged when `i>1 && diff_degrees(cusp, cuspsv).abs() < VERY_SMALL_PLAC_ITER`; track `cuspsv`. If `i` reaches NITER_MAX → NonConverged. On convergence the speed is `asc_dash(rectasc, f, sine, cose)` at the CONVERGED `f`.
2. **Placidus (default arm)** — ref §5 default. `if |fi| >= 90-ekl`: call `fill_porphyry` (from sub-task 2) and return. Else `a=asind(tand(fi)*tane)`; run the helper for cusps 11 (fh1=atand(sind(a/3)/tane), rectasc=degnorm(30+th), divisor=3), 12 (fh2=atand(sind(a*2/3)/tane), 60+th, divisor=1.5), 2 (fh2, 120+th, 1.5), 3 (fh1, 150+th, 3). Any NonConverged → `fill_porphyry` + return (mirrors `goto porphyry`). Mirror fills opposite cusps.
3. **Koch (K)** — ref §5 "K": `if |fi|>=90-ekl` → fill_porphyry+return (no iteration). Else closed-form: `sina=sind(mc)*sine/cosd(fi)` clipped to [-1,1], `cosa=sqrt(1-sina²)`, `c=atand(tanfi/cosa)`, `ad3=asind(sind(c)*sina)/3`; cusps 11/12/2/3 at `th+30-2ad3`, `th+60-ad3`, `th+120+ad3`, `th+150+2ad3` (pole height `fi`); speeds via asc_dash. (Analytical — do_interpol stays false.)
4. **Gauquelin (G)** — ref §5 "G": `if |fi|>=90-ekl` → fill_porphyry+return. Two mirrored loops (ih=2..9 with ih2=10-ih and rectasc=degnorm((90/9)*ih2+th); ih=29..36 with ih2=ih-28 and rectasc=degnorm(180-ih2*90/9+th)), each using the shared helper with `divisor = 9.0/(ih2 as f64)` and `fh_init=atand(sind(a*ih2/9)/tane)`. Fill `cusps[ih]` + opposite `cusps[ih±18]` and their speeds (§5 "G" final block: cusps[1]=ac, [10]=mc, [19]=ac+180, [28]=mc+180). G is in the post-switch-mirror EXCLUSION set (§3 step 3) — do NOT run the 12-cusp mirror for G. `ito=36` for G.

### C reference
`docs/c-ref-houses.md` §5 K/G/Default; §4.2(a); §12.7 (difdeg2n convergence — critical for bit-fidelity). Read swehouse.c:1623–1983 directly if the iteration count diverges from C (FP order in the Newton loop affects which iteration captures `f`).

### Golden tests
- C harness: key `"iterative"` for chars `['P','K']` × battery → `{hsys, armc, geolat, eps, cusps:[1..12], cusp_speed:[1..12]}`; key `"gauquelin36"` for `'G'` × battery → `{armc, geolat, eps, cusps:[1..36], cusp_speed:[1..36]}`. IMPORTANT: include polar-circle geolat (±78 — add to the battery for THIS task only) to verify the Porphyry fallback path. Regenerate houses.json.
- Rust tests `iterative` and `gauquelin36`: cusps eps 1e-9, speeds eps 1e-7 (these are analytical-at-converged-point; if iteration replicates exactly, 1e-9 may pass — try it). Assert the polar cases fall back to Porphyry values (they will match C's Porphyry output through the same fixture).

### Acceptance criteria
- `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean.
- `cargo test --test golden houses::iterative -- --nocapture` passes.
- `cargo test --test golden houses::gauquelin36 -- --nocapture` passes.
- All prior houses tests still pass.

### Escape hatch
Same as sub-task 1. The Newton convergence (count + captured `f`) is the highest-risk fidelity point — if cusps are off by ~1e-6 (≈ VERY_SMALL_PLAC_ITER), the iteration converged one step early/late; read swehouse.c and match the `diff_degrees` test and `cuspsv` update order exactly. Stop after two attempts; escalate to Opus.
execution_record: Codex adversarial review (vidhi-review, combined diff 743f5e9..474b5f1 with swisseph-rs/61) flagged the cap-boundary mismatch; verified directly against swehouse.c (3 call sites, identical `i >= niter_max` semantics) before accepting. Fix: in `placidus_newton_cusp`'s loop, both the degenerate-axis and converged early-returns now check `i >= NITER_MAX` first and `break` to fall through to `NonConverged` instead of returning success, matching C's cap rejection exactly. cargo clippy --all-targets clean; full `cargo test` (77 tests) and the houses golden suite (great_circle, iterative, gauquelin36) pass unchanged. No new golden case added for the exact cap-iteration boundary — golden battery doesn't hit it; flagged as residual gap below.
root_cause: The shared Newton-iteration helper (`placidus_newton_cusp`) ported the convergence-check `for` loop body faithfully but missed that C's post-loop guard `if (i >= niter_max) goto porphyry` (swehouse.c:1667/1865/1901) rejects results obtained on the cap iteration itself, not just true non-convergence. The Rust loop returned `Converged`/`DegenerateAxis` as soon as the in-loop condition was met, with no check on which iteration it was — so convergence landing exactly on i==NITER_MAX shipped a real cusp where C silently falls back to Porphyry.

messages.text:
Implemented Placidus (P, default arm), Koch (K), Gauquelin-36 (G) in calc_h. Shared `placidus_newton_cusp` Newton helper (NewtonCusp enum: Converged{cusp,f}/DegenerateAxis/NonConverged) used by both P and G. All three fall back to fill_porphyry inside the polar circle (|geolat|>=90-eps). Gauquelin sets a new `skip_mirror` flag to exclude itself from the post-switch opposite-cusp mirror only on full 36-cusp convergence (matches C's hsy-reassignment-on-fallback semantics).

Golden battery extended with polar geolats (+-78, eps=23.4392911 -> cutoff ~66.56deg) to exercise the Porphyry fallback. New keys: `iterative` (P/K x 6 armc x 7 geolat = 84 cases) and `gauquelin36` (G x 6 armc x 7 geolat = 42 cases, cusps[1..36] via Vec<f64> since serde's array impl tops out at 32 elements).

All tests passed on first generation/run — no FP-fidelity debugging needed. cargo clippy --all-targets clean, full test suite (80+12+77 tests) green.

Codex review (combined with swisseph-rs/61, diff 743f5e9..474b5f1): needs-attention.

CONFIRMED finding [medium] — Newton convergence cap-boundary mismatch (src/houses.rs:285-297, `placidus_newton_cusp`):
The shared Placidus/Gauquelin Newton loop is `for i in 1..=NITER_MAX { ...; if converged { return Converged } }`. C's loop is `for (i=1; i<=niter_max; i++) { ...; if (converged) break; }` followed by `if (i >= niter_max) { goto porphyry; }`. Because C's post-loop check is `>=` not `>`, C treats convergence achieved exactly on the cap iteration (i==niter_max==100) as a FAILURE and falls back to Porphyry — but the Rust port accepts convergence on i==100 as success. Verified this pattern is identical across all three C call sites (Placidus cusp 11, cusp 12, and Gauquelin's mirrored loops) at swehouse.c:1648-1670, 1850-1869, 1886-1905.

Impact: any cusp that first converges exactly on the 100th Newton iteration will diverge from C — Rust ships the converged Placidus/Gauquelin cusp+speed where C silently falls back to Porphyry (and for Gauquelin, this also wrongly skips the mirror-exclusion path). Most likely near the polar circle where convergence is slow. The golden battery (including the new ±78° polar cases) apparently doesn't hit this exact boundary, since both golden tests pass.

Fix: change the loop to reject convergence on the cap iteration too, e.g. iterate `1..NITER_MAX` (exclusive) for the convergence check, or explicitly return `NonConverged` when `i == NITER_MAX` even if the diff threshold was met — matching C's `i >= niter_max` semantics. Add a boundary-case golden/unit test that forces exactly 100 iterations near-polar to lock this in.

No other findings from Codex's pass (polar-shift subsets R/C/T/H/J, Horizon's recompute+unconditional-180 sequencing, Gauquelin's mirror exclusion, Koch's non-iterative closed form, and calc_h's complexity all checked out). Verdict: request changes — fix the cap-boundary bug before closing.
